open_problems_section.description: Whether the paper has a section devoted to open problems or future work.

extraction_confidence.description: low when the LaTeX was fragmentary, truncated, or hard to read.

key_results.description: Concrete objects and numeric bounds this paper establishes, one short line each. Quantitative only -- vertex counts, orders, thresholds, verified ranges, named constructed objects. These feed the Frontier axis at stage 2.

notes_on_paper.description: Why confidence is low, or anything else about the source as a whole.

statements.description: One entry per distinct open problem. Empty array if the paper states none.

claim.description: One sentence in plain prose stating what would settle THIS problem. Distinguishes Statements that share a verbatim sentence; two Statements with the same claim are the same problem.

verbatim.description: The problem statement copied from the source, LaTeX intact. Never paraphrased.

context.description: Surrounding text needed to interpret the statement. Copied, not summarised.

location.description: Where it sits, as a reader would cite it: 'Conjecture 1.2', 'Section 6, unnumbered'.

environment.description: LaTeX environment name if the statement is in one, else null.

stated_as.description: The paper's own claim about the problem's status.

attribution_kind.description: Who this paper credits the problem to.

attributed_to.description: Name as it appears in THIS paper's text. null if the paper does not say. Never supplied from your own knowledge.

attributed_citation.description: Citation as it appears in THIS paper's text, e.g. '[17]'. null if absent. Never supplied from your own knowledge.

notes.description: Ambiguities resolved, nearby partial results, or reasons for uncertainty.
